**Other information:**

### Problem
When a TreeStore operates with unhydrated raw objects (`autoInitRecords: false`, e.g. Turbo Mode) and a node is re-added via `TreeStore#add` or `TreeStore#splice`, subsequent raw batched row updates (such as `TreeStore#batchRowUpdate`) update `#allRecordsMap` but the authoritative visible row projection in `Collection.Base` continues referencing the stale pre-re-add object reference. When a resort, refilter, or reprojection triggers, the visible row reverts to the old pre-batch values.

### Root Cause
1. In `Collection.Base#splice`, a defensive check `if (!toAddMap || (toAddMap && toAddMap.indexOf(key) < 0))` skipped removing existing keyed items when replacing a key with a new item reference if `toAddMap` contained the key. Because the key remained in `this.map`, the addition loop also skipped inserting the updated object, preventing in-place replacement.
2. In `TreeStore#splice`, when re-adding an existing node (`#allRecordsMap.has(key)`), the existing visible row was not marked in `visibleToRemove`, and the re-added raw object did not preserve existing structural metadata (`isLeaf`, `childCount`, `collapsed`) if omitted from the re-added data literal.

### Solution
1. In `src/collection/Base.mjs`:
   - Removed the `toAddMap` removal-blocking condition so existing items sharing a key with an added item are cleanly evicted from `this.map` and `this.items`, allowing the incoming item to replace the key in place.
2. In `src/data/TreeStore.mjs`:
   - Moved `let existing = me.#allRecordsMap.get(key);` to the start of the addition loop.
   - Preserved existing structural properties (`isLeaf`, `childCount`, `collapsed`) on raw re-adds when not explicitly overridden on the incoming literal.
   - When an existing visible row is being replaced (`existing && existing !== data && me.map.has(key)`), pushed the old visible row into `visibleToRemove` and recorded `insertIndex = me.indexOfKey(key)` so `Collection.Base#splice` updates the visible projection in-place.
3. Added comprehensive unit tests in `test/playwright/unit/data/TreeStoreBatchReprojection.spec.mjs` verifying:
   - Re-add followed by row batch update retains updated field values across `sort()`.
   - Re-add followed by row batch update retains updated field values across filter reprojection.
   - Repeated re-adds preserve sibling and child counts without corruption.
   - Same-object re-add and unhydrated raw batch updates work without premature record hydration.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

- **Challenge**: `Collection.Base#indexOfKey(key)` (`src/collection/Base.mjs:1234-1236`) is implemented as `this._items.indexOf(this.get(key))`. On `Neo.data.Store` and `Neo.data.TreeStore`, `this.get(key)` lazily hydrates raw rows via `hydrateRecord()` (`src/data/Store.mjs:893`, `src/data/TreeStore.mjs:886-919`). Because this PR exposes `me.indexOfKey(key)` on same-key replacements in both `TreeStore#splice` (`:1158`) and `Collection.Base#splice` (`:1585`), even a single raw Turbo Mode re-add (`store.add({id: 'a', ...}, false)`) secretly instantiates a `Record` for the evicted object, and a two-item raw re-add (`store.add([{id: 'a', name: 'A2'}, {id: 'c', name: 'C2'}], false)`) hydrates the stale `c` from `me.map` during `super.splice` and overwrites `#allRecordsMap` and `#childrenMap` back to `'C'`.

### 📋 Required Actions

To proceed with merging, please address the following:

- [ ] **Eliminate hidden `get()` hydration and structural-map overwrite during `splice` eviction (`src/collection/Base.mjs:1234-1236, 1585`, `src/data/TreeStore.mjs:1158`):** `Collection.Base#indexOfKey(key)` calls `this._items.indexOf(this.get(key))`. On `Store` / `TreeStore`, `this.get(key)` runs `hydrateRecord()`, which instantiates a `Record` during raw Turbo Mode `add(..., false)` and — when re-adding 2+ keys such as `store.add([{id: 'a', name: 'A2'}, {id: 'c', name: 'C2'}], false)` on `[a, b, c]` — hydrates the stale `c` from `me.map` inside `super.splice` and overwrites `#allRecordsMap` / `#childrenMap` back to `'C'` (`store.getChildren('root')` returns `'C'` instead of `'C2'`). Resolve indices via `this.map.get(key)` (e.g. `this._items.indexOf(this.map.get(key))`) rather than `this.get(key)` so index lookups and evictions never hydrate or mutate structural maps.
- [ ] **Preserve flat `_items` projection order on multi-item and mixed unsorted re-adds (`src/data/TreeStore.mjs:1154-1160, 1210-1220, 1281`):** `TreeStore#splice` passes a single scalar `insertIndex` to `super.splice(insertIndex, visibleToRemove, visibleToAdd, silent)`. At `d96e471611`, `store.add([{id: 'a', name: 'A2'}, {id: 'c', name: 'C2'}], false)` on unsorted `[a, b, c]` sets `insertIndex = 0` from `'a'` and splices both replacements at `0` (`store.items` becomes `['a', 'c', 'b']` while `#childrenMap` is `['a', 'b', 'c']`), and `store.add([{id: 'a', name: 'A2'}, {id: 'z', name: 'Z'}], false)` on `[a, b]` inserts `'z'` at index `1` (`['a', 'z', 'b']` vs `['a', 'b', 'z']`). Ensure each replaced visible node stays at its structural sibling position and newly added siblings insert at their own `getInsertIndexForNode()` position.
- [ ] **Reconcile visible descendants when re-adding an expanded parent (`src/data/TreeStore.mjs:1147-1160, 1211-1212`):** At `d96e471611`, re-adding an expanded parent `p` (with visible children `[c1, c2]`) as `{id: 'p', name: 'P collapsed', collapsed: true}` evicts only `p` into `visibleToRemove`, leaving `c1, c2` visible in `store.items` under a collapsed parent; re-adding `{id: 'p', name: 'P2'}` (inheriting `collapsed: false`) pushes already-visible `c1, c2` into `visibleToAdd` and emits them again in `mutate.addedItems`. When `existing.collapsed === false` transitions to `data.collapsed === true`, evict `existing`'s visible descendants; when an already-visible parent stays expanded at the same parent/position, replace the parent row without re-adding its already-visible descendants.
- [ ] **Preserve hydrated `Record` identity on re-add and complete AC-4 unit coverage (`src/data/TreeStore.mjs:1116-1170`, `test/playwright/unit/data/TreeStoreBatchReprojection.spec.mjs:118-141`):** At `d96e471611`, if key `'a'` is already a hydrated `Record` (`autoInitRecords: true` or after `const recA = store.get('a')`), calling `store.add({id: 'a', name: 'A2', score: 10})` or `store.add({id: 'a', name: 'A2'}, false)` evicts `recA` from `me.map` / `me._items` and either mints a second `Record` instance (`store.get('a') !== recA`) or demotes the row back to a raw object. When `RecordFactory.isRecord(existing)` and `data !== existing` is a raw literal, update `existing` with the incoming fields (preserving structural defaults when omitted) and keep `existing` as the single `Record` instance across `#allRecordsMap`, `#childrenMap`, and `me.map` / `me._items`. Expand `TreeStoreBatchReprojection.spec.mjs` to assert: (1) hydrated-record re-add preserves `recA` identity and updated values across `updateRows` + `sort`, (2) raw re-add + `updateRows` + `sort`/`filter` invokes zero record hydrations (`store._items.every(item => !RecordFactory.isRecord(item))`), (3) multi-item (`[a, c]`) and mixed (`[a, z]`) unsorted re-adds match `getChildren('root')` order, and (4) expanded-parent re-adds handle both `collapsed: false` retention and `collapsed: true` descendant removal.
